title: Byatarayanapura (AC 152) Sentinel-2 land-cover change, dry season 2019 vs 2026
status: DRAFT - first-pass, unreviewed. Proxies from two single dates, not a land-use survey. Describes land cover only.

boundary.source: DataMeet maps repo, docs/data/geojson/ac.geojson (Assembly Constituencies scraped from ECI polling-station site psleci.nic.in)
boundary.district_note: Bengaluru Urban district; the DataMeet file (OBJECTID 2355) labels it DIST_NAME BANGALORE, PC_NO 24 BANGALORE NORTH
boundary.delimitation: 2008 (Delimitation Order 2008; Karnataka first used it in the 2008 election). Inferred: STATUS field empty (DataMeet marks only pre-delimitation states).
boundary.known_issues: DataMeet README: 'There is some shift in the data'. Polygon has 1 part(s), 76 vertices. Treat edges as approximate.

imagery.collection: sentinel-2-l2a (Microsoft Planetary Computer STAC, anonymous SAS-signed asset URLs)
imagery.selection: All Jan-Mar acquisitions were grouped by date and relative orbit (every one over Byatarayanapura is orbit R019, and the single tile 43PGQ covers the whole boundary, so no mosaic is needed) and scored by the SCL cloud/shadow/no-data fraction inside the boundary on a 60 m grid (data/candidates.json). No February 2019 date is under 0.1% masked here (the lowest is 0.10% on 23 Feb, whose nearest 2026 date, 21 Feb, is 0.75% masked). Chose 13 Feb 2019 (Sentinel-2A; 0.237% masked at 60 m; tile cloud 0.07%) and 11 Feb 2026 (Sentinel-2B; 0.000% masked), two days apart in the calendar, same orbit and tile, and the same dates as the Mahadevapura run on the same tile. Marginally cleaner 2-day pairs exist: 3 Feb 2019/1 Feb 2026 (0.131%/0.000%, but the 2019 tile had 7.3% cloud nearby, raising the risk of unflagged haze) and 24 Jan 2019/22 Jan 2026 (0.154%/0.000%). The masked difference is about 0.1% of the area (~20 ha) and is covered by robustness_check.py. 2026 had clean dates, so no 2025 fallback was needed.

method.grid: EPSG:32643, 10.0 m pixels, 2394x1894; 10 m bands nearest-neighbour, B11 (20 m) bilinear, SCL (20 m) nearest. Same-date tiles mosaicked (first listed tile wins in overlaps).
method.reflectance: L2A (DN + BOA_ADD_OFFSET)/10000; offset -1000 for processing baseline >= 04.00 (decided per tile), 0 before
method.cloud_mask: SCL classes excluded: ['no data', 'saturated/defective', 'cloud shadow', 'cloud medium prob', 'cloud high prob', 'thin cirrus']. Areas counted only on pixels valid in BOTH dates inside the boundary.

thresholds.builtup_bare_proxy: NDBI = (B11-B08)/(B11+B08) > 0 AND NDVI < 0.2 AND not MNDWI water. A PROXY: also catches bare soil, dry/harvested fields, cleared plots, quarries, rock, dry grass

method.note_categories: Categories are independent thresholds; a pixel can be in none of them. They do not sum to 100%.

vegetation_inside_vs_outside_osm_protect.source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass: boundary=protected_area|national_park, leisure=nature_reserve, landuse=forest; "https://overpass-api.de/api/interpreter" queried "2026-11-24T21:42:47+00:00"

water_bodies_osm.query: Overpass API: way/relation natural=water or landuse=reservoir intersecting the boundary polygon, named or not
water_bodies_osm.note: Overpass endpoint https://overpass.kumi.systems/api/interpreter, queried 2026-11-24T21:31:40+00:00; response cached in data/osm_water_all.json and reused. Water ha = pixels with MNDWI>0 inside the OSM outline (clipped to the boundary); measured only if >= 2.0 ha. Water bodies covered by weeds count as vegetation. OSM outlines are volunteer-drawn and current-day; overlapping OSM features (e.g. a river polygon and a reservoir polygon) are listed separately and can double count.
water_bodies_osm.green_on_lake_note: vegetation_ha_<year> on each water body is 'green on lake': NDVI>0.4 pixels inside the OSM outline. On urban lakes this is mostly floating weeds (e.g. water hyacinth) or reeds, which hide open water from the MNDWI test, so water and green should be read together.

totals_measured_water_bodies.note: Union of the outlines of all measured water bodies (overlaps counted once), pixels valid in both dates.

new_bare_or_builtup_proxy_clusters.definition: 4-connected regions of pixels that were NOT built-up/bare proxy on 13 Feb 2019 (vegetation or other non-bare cover) and ARE built-up/bare proxy on 11 Feb 2026, valid in both dates, inside the boundary. Label: 'new bare or built-up ground (proxy)'. Each could be a quarry, construction, a cleared or ploughed field, harvested cropland, dry grass or burnt vegetation or a drained water body; this analysis does not and cannot say which, nor anything about cause, ownership or legality.
new_bare_or_builtup_proxy_clusters.nbr_note: NBR = (B08-B12)/(B08+B12); dNBR = NBR(first date) - NBR(second date), median over the cluster. Reported only as a spectral descriptor: dNBR above ~0.1 is commonly read in the literature as a possible recent-burn signal, but dry soil, harvest and clearing can also raise it. Unverified; no ground truth.
